architecture.mechanism: Stochastic Rate and Recovery (SRR) method combined with Monte Carlo simulation to model probabilistic soiling profiles and optimize cleaning frequency.
architecture.intervention: Deploy a site-specific data-driven model using the SRR method to predict soiling dynamics and identify high-risk zones (lower row edges), enabling targeted, variable-interval cleaning schedules that optimize the limited 0.5 L/panel water budget.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduction of soiling losses from 12-18% by aligning the two manual cleaning visits with the predicted peak soiling windows, thereby maximizing energy yield without exceeding water or labor constraints.
architecture.falsification_test: Implement the model for one season and compare actual annual yield loss against the model's prediction; if the actual loss exceeds the model's projected loss by more than 2%, the mechanism is considered ineffective for this specific desert edge topology.
